title: Small Fourier Deficit Implies Closeness to a Dictator
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube. Suppose $0\leq\delta\leq 1/1600$ and the sum of the squared level-one Fourier coefficients of the real-valued version of $f$ is $1-\delta$. Then some coordinate dictator, or its negation, differs from $f$ on at most a fraction $1601\delta$ of the inputs.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
The level-one Fourier weight of the real-valued version of $f$ equals $1-\delta$
